input.summary:
Bin store furnished in parts/room-4.mjs (2 wide x 12 long, y 7..12): crates and hay stacked on the east wall, iron_bars bicycle rail, a focal crate-and-hay stack at the south end, the x 24 lane clear from the rear door to the lobby.
Light: 2 hanging lanterns under the landing floor and 2 standing on crates; `mcd room` says OK, min light 8, mean 11.2, 0 dark cells, walk reaches every free floor cell. make.sh whole, room-4 line 18 placed with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE.
Structure check: no floating or unsupported blocks in the bin store; the 8 orphans it reports are elsewhere in the build.
left: Palette has no barrel, chest, candle or bed, so the bins are dark_oak_planks crates and hay bales; the spec's barrels and candles would need palette.json entries first.
No tool shows the interior from inside the closed shell: room.png's cutaway and the zoom both show walls, so the furniture was checked by the floor grid and light numbers, not by eye.

The plan's floor grid marks the x 23 column (z 3..13) as open 'D', so the bin store has no west wall of its own and opens onto the stair bay. The stair part must keep x 23 clear at the foot of the flight or the room opens up there.
Did not tick elements.md 'Light: all rooms >= 8' (a whole-building item); the bin store meets it (min 8) and the lamplighter should confirm the other rooms.

waste.what: Drew the furniture cell by cell as 12-character rows per layer, then fixed a row index by hand (the hanging lanterns landed on z 3 and z 8 instead of z 4 and z 9).
waste.cost: 2 rewrites of the layer rows and one Edit; about 6 layers x 12 rows typed by hand
waste.tool: A layers() form that takes coordinates per block (e.g. a list of [x,y,z,block,state]) or a plan output that marks the row index beside each z, so a wrong row shows up before the build

waste.what: Found the lamp spots by trial: placed 4 lanterns, ran make.sh and mcd room, then read the light grid.
waste.cost: 1 make.sh and 1 room check; no lamp count was computed beforehand
waste.tool: mcd room's lantern spots output (already printed as LAMPS) could be fed back into the furnisher as a list to place in the same pass, so lamps are chosen before the first build

waste.what: Looked for the furniture in room.png and zoom.png; both views are closed by the shell, so the interior could not be checked by eye.
waste.cost: 2 renders, neither readable for the interior
waste.tool: mcd rooms or zoom with a cut at the room's top (--cut y) and an eye view from the entrance, so the furnished interior is visible

companions.task: Build the bicycle rail and crate stacks in dark_oak as proper joinery, with the iron_bars connections set, so the rail reads as a fitting rather than loose posts.
Check the whole building's light for the other rooms and decide whether the bin store's 4 lanterns can be cut to 3 without going under 8 at the rear door.

structured_output.summary:
Bin store furnished in parts/room-4.mjs (2 wide x 12 long, y 7..12): crates and hay stacked on the east wall, iron_bars bicycle rail, a focal crate-and-hay stack at the south end, the x 24 lane clear from the rear door to the lobby.
Light: 2 hanging lanterns under the landing floor and 2 standing on crates; `mcd room` says OK, min light 8, mean 11.2, 0 dark cells, walk reaches every free floor cell. make.sh whole, room-4 line 18 placed with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE.
Structure check: no floating or unsupported blocks in the bin store; the 8 orphans it reports are elsewhere in the build.
left: Palette has no barrel, chest, candle or bed, so the bins are dark_oak_planks crates and hay bales; the spec's barrels and candles would need palette.json entries first.
No tool shows the interior from inside the closed shell: room.png's cutaway and the zoom both show walls, so the furniture was checked by the floor grid and light numbers, not by eye.

The plan's floor grid marks the x 23 column (z 3..13) as open 'D', so the bin store has no west wall of its own and opens onto the stair bay. The stair part must keep x 23 clear at the foot of the flight or the room opens up there.
Did not tick elements.md 'Light: all rooms >= 8' (a whole-building item); the bin store meets it (min 8) and the lamplighter should confirm the other rooms.

waste.what: Drew the furniture cell by cell as 12-character rows per layer, then fixed a row index by hand (the hanging lanterns landed on z 3 and z 8 instead of z 4 and z 9).
waste.cost: 2 rewrites of the layer rows and one Edit; about 6 layers x 12 rows typed by hand
waste.tool: A layers() form that takes coordinates per block (e.g. a list of [x,y,z,block,state]) or a plan output that marks the row index beside each z, so a wrong row shows up before the build

waste.what: Found the lamp spots by trial: placed 4 lanterns, ran make.sh and mcd room, then read the light grid.
waste.cost: 1 make.sh and 1 room check; no lamp count was computed beforehand
waste.tool: mcd room's lantern spots output (already printed as LAMPS) could be fed back into the furnisher as a list to place in the same pass, so lamps are chosen before the first build

waste.what: Looked for the furniture in room.png and zoom.png; both views are closed by the shell, so the interior could not be checked by eye.
waste.cost: 2 renders, neither readable for the interior
waste.tool: mcd rooms or zoom with a cut at the room's top (--cut y) and an eye view from the entrance, so the furnished interior is visible
